first.rationale: All 10 tasks failed with plan_length 0 and executed_actions 0 (e_6d2b1f3f5bafe15a, e_d5ba2587d191ff0e) despite non-empty goals, so the earliest observed failure is that get_plan never emitted a plan. Two concrete bugs in the incumbent explain this: (1) the object scan `for n, t in objects` iterates a set of tuples as if it were (name, type) pairs after unpacking - that part is fine - but the initial-state loop assigned spanner locations into the same dict keys used for man detection (`who in spanner_locs or who in spanners`), which misclassifies facts; (2) crucially `apply` read the tighten nut as `action[4]` while the internal tuple is ("tighten_nut", loc, spanner, man, nut) so index 4 is indeed the nut - however the pickup branch did `del sp_locs[s]` on a KeyError-prone dict and the walker returned formatted strings, so any exception inside BFS aborted get_plan and the runner recorded a 0-length plan (plan_semantics). I rewrote the planner to avoid the mutating/copying fragility: all state transitions build fresh dicts explicitly per branch, action grounding is generated from explicit index positions, and the returned plan is always list[str] via a generic formatter, so no internal representation leaks. Goal checking uses the goal's own tightened atoms rather than assuming every nut is a goal. This should make executed_actions > 0 and produce valid VAL-checkable plans.
